title: Engineering Rhodotorula toruloides as a platform organism for de novo synthesis of fatty-acid esters
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75029-1

Fatty acid esters are biofuels, eco-friendly detergents, and cosmetic emollients, however, their industrial production is unsustainable. Here the authors develop a de novo biosynthesis platform using the yeast Rhodotorula toruloides and achieve high-level production of structurally diverse esters.

title: Warming climate has lengthened global intense tropical cyclone seasons
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74651-3

Under ongoing climate change, global intense tropical cyclone seasons have become longer. The rising frequency of off-season intense tropical cyclones increases human exposure to destructive storm hazards outside historical seasonal norms.

title: FET proteins and PARylation-dependent condensates promote replication fork reversal and genome stability
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74950-9

FUS, EWSR1 and TAF15 function in a variety of cellular processes by forming biomolecular condensates. Here the authors reveal that these proteins respond to replication stress to promote fork reversal, maintain genome stability, and support the viability of BRCA1-deficient cancer cells.

title: TRPC4/TRPC5 are critical for neuronal modulation by transcranial focused ultrasound in retrosplenial cortex in male mice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74779-2

The authors find that transcranial focused ultrasound non-invasively modulates Egr1+ neuronal activity via TRPC4 and TRPC5 channels in the retrosplenial cortex in male mice, regulating mechanical and thermal sensitivity.

title: Nur77 agonism invigorates Natural Killer cell immunity against hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75027-3

Nuclear receptor Nur77 is a transcription factor with immunomodulatory functions. Here, by integrating patient-derived samples, organoid co-cultures, and mouse models of hepatocellular carcinoma, the authors show that Nur77 promotes NK cell maturation and cytotoxicity by reducing lipid-mediated suppression and upregulating AP-1 response gene, and that Nur-77 agonism improves the response to adoptive NK cell therapy in HCC preclinical mouse models.

title: Targeting the Ip6k2–Runx2 axis disrupts osteoblast–osteoclast coupling to treat osteoporosis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75098-2

The study shows that Ip6k2 partners with Runx2 to drive osteoclast activity. Targeting Ip6k2 selectively reduces bone resorption, increases bone mass, and protects against osteoporosis without affecting bone formation.

title: Impaired IFNγ responsiveness of monocyte-derived lung cells limits immunity to Mycobacterium tuberculosis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75096-4

Mycobacterium tuberculosis can persist in the lung. This study shows that permissive monocyte derived lung cells fail to respond to IFNγ and that prior immunity overcomes this defect, boosting cell responsiveness and improving lung bacterial control.

title: Tropical origins of the recent trends in Northern Hemisphere wintertime jet streams
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74980-3

This study shows that the recent trends in the North Pacific and the North Atlantic jet streams in winter are linked to an increased number of intense North Pacific precipitation events, which are in turn favored by tropical Pacific precipitation trends.
